title: Ask Instead of Answer — Supporting Children's Ideas
audience: Teachers and parents of 6–10 year olds

slides.title: Two skills, practised in pairs
slides.headline: Ask before answering · Separate dreaming from checking
body: Everything is voluntary — you can observe instead
This is a learning format we are trying, not therapy
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome. Agenda in one sentence. Ground rules: voluntary, not therapy, phones away for 45 minutes.

slides.title: "That can't work"
slides.headline: Remember a moment when a quick answer stopped an idea
body: Pair-share, 3 minutes
One line each from a few volunteers
slides.audience_prompt: Turn to your neighbour: a moment when an adult's quick answer stopped an idea — yours or a child's.
slides.speaker_notes: Introduce the three common adult replies. Run the pair-share. Collect two or three one-liners. Bridge: what could the adult have said instead?

slides.title: Module 1 — Ask instead of answer
slides.headline: When we ask, the child keeps authorship
body: The adult asks; the child decides
slides.speaker_notes: One minute: why questions keep the child as the author of the idea.

slides.title: Three questions and one loop
slides.headline: What exactly? · Compared to what? · How will you know?
body: Goal → try → re-check → continue or finish
The child makes the last call
slides.speaker_notes: Model each question with one child sentence: 'I want a huge house' — huge compared to what? Then walk the loop with the bridge-between-two-towers example.

slides.title: Practice: questions only
slides.headline: Partner A is the child with an idea card; partner B may only ask
body: 3.5 minutes, then swap
No solutions, no suggestions — only questions
slides.audience_prompt: Pick an idea card. B: ask, don't answer.
slides.speaker_notes: Hand out idea cards. Time two rounds of 3.5 minutes. Walk around; note good questions to quote in the debrief.

slides.title: Debrief
slides.headline: What changed when you could not give the answer?
body: What was hard?
What did the 'child' do that surprised you?
Limit: one round tells us little — this is practice, not proof
slides.speaker_notes: Collect two observations. Name the limit: one round shows a feel, not an effect.

slides.title: Module 2 — Dreamer, Realist, Critic
slides.headline: Big ideas often get criticised before they exist
body: Separate the moments, protect the idea
slides.speaker_notes: One minute: questions help detail an idea; but some ideas die before they form.

slides.title: Three rooms
slides.headline: Dream without critique · Plan the steps · Check what's missing
body: The Critic critiques the plan, never the person
An assumption worth testing, not a proven method
slides.speaker_notes: Explain each room with one question. Say clearly that this structure is a working assumption.

slides.title: Practice: walk the rooms
slides.headline: Trios rotate roles on one child idea — 3 minutes per room
body: Dreamer: 'What else could it do?'
Realist: 'What do we build first?'
Critic: 'What's missing — and how do we protect the idea?'
slides.audience_prompt: In trios, take one idea card through all three rooms.
slides.speaker_notes: Time three rounds. Remind Critics to praise specific choices, not labels.

slides.title: Debrief
slides.headline: Which room do you usually start in with children?
body: What happens to ideas if we start in the Critic's room?
Risk: rooms become rigid — children move between them
slides.speaker_notes: Two or three answers. Bridge: how will you use this on Monday?

slides.title: One week, one question
slides.headline: Pick one situation where you will ask before you answer
body: Fill in your transfer card (2 min)
Limit: we don't yet know whether this changes creativity long term
Your notes are personal observations, not research data — share only if you wish
Closing round: one word each
slides.audience_prompt: Write one situation and one question you will try this week.
slides.speaker_notes: Transfer card, then the honest limit, then the optional sharing invitation with consent, then a closing word round.
